The one substantive repeat is mem_normalizer_of_subgroupOf. The repo already has the same lemma with the same proof in several files. I read Goldschmidt75/Closure.lean (generic, `Type*`, no Finite), Item812Res12ProofIrred.lean (also `Type`-universe) and checked the duplicate list from grep. findings.excerpt:
private theorem mem_normalizer_of_subgroupOf {Y : Type*} [Group Y] {N S : Subgroup Y}
    (hSN : S ≤ N) {b : N}
findings.problem: This private lemma re-proves a generic fact: if b ∈ N normalizes S.subgroupOf N, then (b : Y) normalizes S. The proof uses the same two-direction normalizer argument as at least two other copies in the repo. In the reverse direction it shows that h lies in N by conjugating back with b⁻¹ and b. `CFSG.Goldschmidt75.mem_normalizer_of_mem_normalizer_subgroupOf` has exactly this statement, with `Type*` and no Finite assumption, and `Item812Res12.mem_normalizer_of_subgroupOf` has it too. Other near-duplicates exist in Goldschmidt/Steps/G310Basic.lean and CentralizerFrattiniSplit.lean. The reverse-direction membership argument (`h ∈ N` via `N.mul_mem (N.mul_mem (N.inv_mem b.2) ...) b.2`) is therefore maintained in several places. Each copy is a chance for the proofs to drift apart.
findings.proposed_change: Delete the private lemma and the shared copy's duplicates. Use one shared lemma, for example the existing `CFSG.Goldschmidt75.mem_normalizer_of_mem_normalizer_subgroupOf`, whose statement is `{S S₀ : Subgroup G} (hle : S₀ ≤ S) {s : S} (hs : s ∈ normalizer ((S₀.subgroupOf S : Subgroup S) : Set S)) : (s : G) ∈ normalizer (S₀ : Set G)`. Add `public import CFSG.Goldschmidt75.Closure`, or move the lemma to a low-level group-theory file if that import is too heavy or cyclic. At the use site, `mem_normalizer_of_subgroupOf hSN hb` in `hdec` (line 219) becomes `CFSG.Goldschmidt75.mem_normalizer_of_mem_normalizer_subgroupOf hSN hb`. The hypotheses match: hSN : S ≤ N and hb : b ∈ normalizer ((S.subgroupOf N : Subgroup N) : Set N). The only other client is this one call, so no other proof in the file changes. The other duplicates (Item812Res12, G310Basic, CentralizerFrattiniSplit) could be switched to the same lemma in the same cleanup.
findings.benefit: The inverse-conjugation membership argument has one proof instead of three or more near-identical ones. A fix or generalisation then applies everywhere. This file also becomes about 15 lines shorter, which leaves the K518 reduction focused on the p-element argument.
